markup:
For a big family room where people sit across a wide sofa or in chairs off to the sides, **a matte white projector screen with a 180° viewing angle is usually the best choice.**

The key is choosing the right screen material, not just the brand.

## Best screen types for wide viewing angles

| Screen type | Typical advertised viewing angle | Best use |
|---|---|---|
| **Matte white (1.0 gain)** | 160°–180° | Widest seating arrangements |
| Acoustically transparent matte white | 160°–180° | Large home theaters with speakers behind screen |
| High-quality gray screen | 120°–180° | Rooms with some ambient light |
| ALR (ambient light rejecting) | 80°–160° | Brighter rooms, but often narrower viewing |
| High-gain screen (1.5+) | Often narrower | Viewers seated near the center |

One important detail: a manufacturer's 180° rating doesn't mean the image stays equally bright from every angle. Matte white screens generally have the most uniform off-axis brightness.
